title: His Hair Caught Fire. He Kept Dancing.
description:
Take six of a 1984 commercial shoot went wrong in seconds.

• Jan 27, 1984 — Shrine Auditorium, Los Angeles
• Pyrotechnics fired early; sparks set Michael Jackson's hair alight
• Second- and third-degree burns to his scalp
• He gave his $1.5M Pepsi settlement to Brotman Medical Center, whose burn center was named for him

Sources:
- UPI via The Michigan Daily (Jan 29, 1984): https://digital.bentley.umich.edu/midaily/mdp.39015071754738/213
- CBS News: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jackson-getting-burned-the-video-surfaces
- Rolling Stone: https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/michael-jackson-pepsi-ad-footage-raises-questions-about-directors-role-in-accident-252777/
- TheWrap: https://www.thewrap.com/michael-jacksons-tragic-pepsi-commercial-accident-unearthed-4324
- Wikipedia (Philanthropy of Michael Jackson): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philanthropy_of_Michael_Jackson

pinned_comment: Accounts say he didn't realize at first and kept moving for a few seconds. Would you have noticed? 👇
notes: Performer drawn as a generic engine figure (no likeness, no signature outfit). No logos; 'Pepsi' only as text. 'Kept dancing': CBS News says about ten seconds; American Songwriter says he reached the bottom and began a twirl before realizing; script says he reached the bottom and spun. Tackle: Rolling Stone (LAFD captain grabbed him and took him down) and CBS (Taraborrelli: 'everybody went down on top of him'). UPI 1984 also cites a witness saying he pulled off his jacket to put out the fire; the cover over his head on screen is symbolic. Burns: UPI 1984 (second-degree + small third-degree on the back of his head), Wikipedia (scalp). $1.5M settlement donated to Brotman Medical Center, burn center named for him: TheWrap + Wikipedia (citing LA Times 1988). Later painkiller/health claims deliberately left out.
caption_instagram:
His hair was on fire. And he kept dancing. 🔥

January 27, 1984: on take six of a commercial shoot in Los Angeles, the pyrotechnics fired early. He gave his entire $1.5M settlement to the hospital that treated him.
